identity.name: Sodium tartrates
identity.chemical_class: Sodium salts of tartaric acid (tartrate salts)

function.mechanism: Tartrate anions buffer acidity and can complex metal ions; in CFR sodium tartrate is listed for emulsification and pH control uses.

adi.basis: EFSA FAF 2020 group ADI for L(+)-tartaric acid-tartrates (E334-337, E354), expressed as tartaric acid.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation reported no genotoxic concern, no carcinogenicity signal in chronic rat data, and refined non-brand-loyal exposure estimates below the group ADI.

adi.basis: WHO/JECFA group ADI 0-30 mg/kg bw for L(+)-tartaric acid and sodium, potassium, potassium sodium salts (expressed as tartaric acid), reaffirmed in 2017 entry.

concerns.summary: High-dose animal data with related tartrate salts (DL-potassium hydrogen tartrate) showed obstructive nephropathy in F344 rats, indicating potential renal hazard at sufficiently high exposure.

A sodium-tartrate-containing iron complex (FemTA) produced GI inflammatory and clinical chemistry effects at mid/high doses in rats, interpreted by authors as iron-overload related rather than tartrate-specific toxicity.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2020 found no genotoxic signal and no carcinogenicity indication for monosodium L(+)-tartrate in chronic rat study conditions.
FDA lists sodium tartrate as a direct food substance affirmed as GRAS under 21 CFR 184.1801 with GMP-limited use.
No sodium tartrate-specific IARC carcinogenic classification was identified in the IARC classification dataset checked.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported refined non-brand-loyal exposure estimates below its group ADI; no retrieved dataset in this run showed population-level exceedance for E335.

risk_assessment.rationale: E335 remains permitted by EFSA/FDA/JECFA with defined ADIs and no strong human-relevant toxicity signal at typical food-use conditions. Concern evidence is mainly from high-dose or related-salt animal studies.
key_factors: EFSA 2020 group ADI of 240 mg/kg bw/day and no refined-scenario exceedance
FDA GRAS status under 21 CFR 184.1801 with GMP conditions
JECFA group ADI 0-30 mg/kg bw for tartaric acid and sodium/potassium tartrate salts
No IARC listing for sodium tartrate/tartaric acid as a classified carcinogenic agent
High-dose renal findings in related tartrate-salt rat studies
